title: Probe into 15 July GCE "O" Level English Oral Exam Incident, Lessons Learnt and Support for Affected Candidates
what_it_is: Probe into 15 July GCE "O" Level English Oral Exam Incident, Lessons Learnt and Support for Affected Candidates

sections.label: Questions on O Level oral exam
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about reviewing the 15 July 2026 O Level English oral examination, assistance requests and remedies for anomalies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in respect of the "O" Level English Language oral examination conducted on 15 July 2026, whether the Ministry intends to review and improve the way the oral examination is conducted notwithstanding the Singapore Examinations and Assessment Board's finding that there was no discrepancy in the question displayed on the candidates’ and examiners' screens, to minimise risks of students being unnecessarily affected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education with respect to the "O" Level English Language oral examination conducted on 15 July 2026 (a) whether any requests for assistance from students or their parents have been received by Singapore Examinations and Assessment Board (SEAB) due to the alleged discrepancy between the question displayed on the candidates’ and the examiners’ screens; and (b) if so, how has SEAB been assisting these students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education before the 2026 "O" Level English results are finalised (a) whether the Singapore Examinations and Assessment Board (SEAB) will compare candidates’ scores and responses from the 15 July 2026 oral session against other sessions; and (b) what remedies will apply if this shows a material session-level or examination-centre-level anomaly despite SEAB’s finding that one version of the examination video and questions was released.

sections.label: Candidates reporting prompt discrepancy
sections.summary: On 15 July 2026, 173 candidates from 76 schools reported a different prompt on their screens, rising to 432 from 102 schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Why do you say so?" On the day of the examination, 173 candidates from 76 different schools reported that the prompt for the planned response segment displayed on their screen at the silent preparation station was different from the one that was posed by the oral examiners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In the following days, the number of candidates who reported similar issues concerning the 15 July oral examination increased to 432 from 102 schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Close to 5,000 candidates sat for the GCE "O" Level English language oral examination on 15 July 2026.

sections.label: Screens matched approved materials
sections.summary: The investigation showed that the prompt on the candidates' screens matched the prompt in the approved examination materials.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The investigation showed that the prompt on the candidates' screens match the prompt in the approved examination materials.

sections.label: Cause not technical or malicious
sections.summary: SEAB concluded the cause of the incidents was neither technical in nature nor a deliberate or malicious act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: SEAB has concluded the cause of these incidents was not technical in nature, nor the result of a deliberate or malicious act.

sections.label: Mean scores comparable
sections.summary: Preliminary data shows the 15 July oral mean score was comparable to the other four 2026 sessions and to the remaining candidates' mean score.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The preliminary data shows that the mean score for the oral examination on 15 July is comparable to that of the other four sessions in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In addition, the mean score of the 432 candidates who reported the prompt discrepancy is also comparable to the mean score of the remaining candidates who sat for the oral examination on 15 July 2026.

sections.label: Review of oral prompt reading
sections.summary: SEAB will review the oral examination processes for students to read the oral prompt more carefully during the 10-minute preparation time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: SEAB will review the oral examination processes for students to read the oral prompt more carefully during the 10-minute preparation time.

sections.label: Updating special consideration applicants
sections.summary: Applicants for special consideration will be updated and engaged on the process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And in such an instance, what will be the process taken and whether the students who had put in the appeal would eventually be updated that their results have taken in the circumstances that had transpired?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Certainly, the applicants for special consideration will be updated and engaged on the process.

sections.label: SEAB learning from misread prompts
sections.summary: SEAB will learn from the incident to reduce misread prompts and better guide exam preparation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, very thorough from a from a technical perspective.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I would point out that his 8% to 9% is on that that day – I presume he is taking the 432 divided by 5,000 – but that was for that day only.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The total number, of course, of people taking the examination across the four days is approximately four times as many.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Yes, indeed, SEAB will look to learn from this incident how we can reduce the risk of prompts being misread, guide the students about the preparation better, both in terms of the preparation for the exam and during the exam itself.

sections.label: External investigation of SEAB evidence
sections.summary: Planning sheets often lacked candidates' names, making correlation with specific reports hard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And supplementary question three: since SEAB has all the evidence needed – the login logs, the examiners' marking comments, the contemporaneous planning sheets, as well as the audio from the session – will the Ministry allow someone outside SEAB to look at them to conduct an external investigation?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is hard to correlate those with specific reports because many of the contemporaneous planning sheets did not have candidates' names written on them; that is not a requirement.

sections.label: GovTech audit of technical platforms
sections.summary: GovTech audited the technical platforms and processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, we have had GovTech come in to audit the technical platforms, the processes and so forth.

sections.label: Examiners trained in positive marking
sections.summary: Examiners are trained in a process of positive marking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The examiners are trained in a process of positive marking.
